questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I love Amsterdam. Wanted to try and live there. Also it was important for me to be somewhere with a biking culture, since this is the only means of transportation I actually enjoy. Academically, I was also attracted to their econometrics courses - unfortunately they would not let me take those as an exchange student, which they only informed me of last minute . After I had been accepted to said courses.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I loved the city. Amsterdam gets a 10. UvA was unfortunately not a very good university and it gets a 2. People were nice there, but the courses were generally of very poor quality - and a major part of students barely spoke any english, despite it being an english programme. This lowered the academic level substantially.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Fairly easy. UvA keeps you updated - possibly too much. They send an endless array of mails that could be summarised in fewer and shorter mails.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Good student desk. They are very helpful and fairly easy to locate.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: The intro programme for exchange students only lasted 1-2 hours. This isn't a lot, and maybe they should do more to welcome people.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Hard. No.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It rains a lot in Amsterdam.

Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I can't really recall it. Was there any?

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Already answered this.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Not at all, as described above. UvA let me choose econometrics courses (that I was even academically pre-approved by UvA, based on documentation they had me spend time on collecting), but then later informed me that I couldn't enroll in them after all - so I had to choose courses that had nothing to do with my academic profile. As a student from UCPH (where economics is not seperate from econometrics) it is impossible to get into the econometrics programme at UvA - so if you're an econometrics student at UCPH they have very few relevant courses for you at UvA, at least at the master's.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't know.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Very low quality: Many of the classes consisted of student presentations of very poor quality; and they were mandatory, so I spent several hours a week listening to people who had no idea of what they were doing. This was made way worse by the clear lack of english speaking skills in many of the foreign students.  Courses were also incredibly chaotic: you have 10.000 different pieces of information lying around in different places on Canvas and an online schedule that regularly gave you wrong information! How hard is it to make a schedule? I have never experienced anything so poorly administrated and executed in my education before UvA.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Mandatory classes consisting of student presentations. Woorks very poorly as described above. Almost all courses focused on remembering points from a handful of academic papers for the 2-3-hour exam. People just got ChatGPT to summarise the main points from these, learned nothing, and passed the exam. Courses and exams were overall without any independent thought or practical usefulnees. I acquired no tools. This was very different from most courses at UCPH, where papers are usually only a (small) part of the exam.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Managerial Economics, Markets and Organisations, Behavioural Economics, Advanced Industrial Organisation, Empirical Market Analysis and Experimental Economics.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Absolutely none of the above.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: UvA has a lot of non-academic offers. Their sport centers are actually pretty good and have fun classes.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Cheap gym membership with regular training classes - lots on offer. Also you can follow specific programs for a small fee as a student. I got 2,5 months of calisthenics courses (really fun) for approx. 50 euro.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Sports

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Visit other cities in NL. Also their museums are really good.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Find good groups to study with. It is difficult, and often the groups are decided by the lecturer, which makes it even harder. But try anyway. Working together really works.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Directness

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Don't count on a challenge. Spend time on campus. Sign up for activities.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: See above

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Trying something new

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Overcoming the incredible boredom derived from my courses
